rfi.title: Macron opens Bayeux Tapestry exhibition before first Burnham talks
rfi.description: French President Emmanuel Macron begins a two-day visit to Britain on Wednesday, opening a landmark exhibition of the Bayeux Tapestry, the 11th-century embroidery depicting the Norman conquest of England, before holding his first in-depth talks with new Prime Minister Andy Burnham on Thursday.

rfi.title: France-UK deal linked to seven-year low in Channel migrant crossings
rfi.description: France and the UK saw the number of small boats carrying migrants across the English Channel fall to its lowest summer level since 2019, with London crediting a new enforcement deal between the two countries.

rfi.title: Nepal glacier disaster toll passes 1,000 as calls for climate justice grow
rfi.description: The death toll from last week's devastating Himalayan glacial floods passed 1,000 on Tuesday, as Chinese and Nepali teams searched for survivors. Nepal's foreign minister said the disaster was "a warning signal" of the growing risks posed by climate change.

rfi.title: DRC school year begins amid Ebola, strikes and conflict
rfi.description: Millions of students returned to school across the Democratic Republic of Congo on Tuesday, but the new term began amid an Ebola outbreak affecting six provinces, a teachers’ strike call and continuing conflict in the east. In AFC/M23-controlled territories, the movement organised the return to classrooms even as Kinshasa continued to pay primary and secondary school teachers.

rfi.title: French clubs cash in as Ligue 1 transfer window comes to a close
rfi.description: The transfer window for French football clubs closed on Tuesday evening after three months of trading that saw the 18 Ligue 1 sides splash out €522 million and reap €894 million in player sales.

rfi.title: French schools start new year in shadow of summer cyberattack
rfi.description: Millions of pupils are returning to classrooms across France on Tuesday for the start of the new school year, with some schools forced to fall back on paper timetables and registers after a major cyberattack disrupted education systems over the summer.

rfi.title: Russia’s return to G20 talks unsettles Europe as Iran and trade tensions loom
rfi.description: Russia's presence at the opening of G20 meetings in North Carolina sparked pushback from Europe on Monday, adding fresh tension to talks already clouded by the Iran war and US President Donald Trump's trade policies.

rfi.title: Ukraine air defences top agenda as EU ministers meet in Ireland
rfi.description: European Union defence and foreign ministers gathering in Ireland this week are set to focus on strengthening Ukraine’s air defences, as concern grows over both Russia’s intensifying bombardment and what European officials see as a widening campaign of destabilisation across the continent.

rfi.title: France takes aim at fast-fashion giants with new pricing penalties
rfi.description: France will start imposing fees on ultra-fast fashion from Tuesday, with charges set to rise to almost €20 per garment as the government steps up pressure on major Asian e-commerce platforms including Shein.

rfi.title: From labels to Netflix, how Quebec's fight to protect French collides with US trade
rfi.description: French-language protections in Quebec have emerged as an unlikely source of friction between Canada and the United States, bringing rules designed to protect French in overwhelmingly English-speaking North America into a much bigger fight over trade.

rfi.title: No more Messi nights for Argentina as skipper says adios to national squad
rfi.description: Fifa president Gianni Infantino led the tributes to Argentina skipper Lionel Messi, who announced his retirement from international football just over a month after playing in the 2026 World Cup final.

rfi.title: 'Devoted servant of the nation': Former French PM Édouard Balladur dies aged 97
rfi.description: Former French prime minister Édouard Balladur died in Paris late Monday at the age of 97, his family said. Born in Turkey, he served as former president Francois Mitterrand's last prime minister from March 1993 to May 1995, carrying out several major privatisations of state companies, and unsuccessfully ran for the top job in 1995.

rfi.title: Ten years after Gabon’s post-election violence, painful questions remain
rfi.description: Ten years on, victims of violence that followed president Ali Bongo’s disputed re-election in Gabon are still demanding truth and justice. Questions also remain over the possible involvement of French nationals and the response of the French authorities.

rfi.title: Niger coup attempt: 'Russians saved the day' analyst tells RFI
rfi.description: Niger’s military government has survived its most serious internal challenge since seizing power in 2023, after Russian paramilitaries helped loyalist forces crush last Saturday's attempted coup in the capital, Niamey. RFI spoke to an expert who explains how this episode has left General Abdourahamane Tiani’s junta weakened and more dependent on Russia.

rfi.title: French high schools scramble to work out rules as phone ban takes effect
rfi.description: The new school year starts on Tuesday in France, and with it comes a new rule: mobile phones will no longer be allowed in high schools. The ban came into force a week before the first day of term, leaving schools with little time to work out how to put it into practice.

rfi.title: France's international photojournalism festival founder Leroy dies aged 69
rfi.description: Tributes have been pouring in for Jean-François Leroy, the founder of the Visa pour l'image photojournalism festival, who died on Monday at the age of 69.

rfi.title: UN committee presents legal case for broad slavery reparations
rfi.description: Countries are "legally obliged" to provide broad reparations for harms resulting from both direct and indirect involvement in the transatlantic African slave trade, a United Nations committee has said. This comes amid a fresh interpretation of a global accord, published on Monday.

rfi.title: What the SDF’s dissolution means for Syria’s Kurds and neighbouring Turkey
rfi.description: Nearly a week after the Syrian Democratic Forces agreed to dissolve, the consequences are beginning to take shape for Syria's Kurds and neighbouring Turkey. As the former US-backed force is absorbed into the Syrian state, questions remain over what the country's Kurds have secured in return – from language and political rights to protections for women – and what the end of more than a decade of Kurdish-led autonomy means for Turkey's own conflict with Kurdish militants.

euronews.title: Weight-loss pill 'Wegovy' on sale in German pharmacies from 1 September
euronews.description: The weight-loss drug Wegovy is now sold in German pharmacies. Semaglutide helps you feel full. It is approved for adults and costs 170-280 euros.

euronews.title: Macron to be first EU leader to meet Andy Burnham during London trip for Bayeux Tapestry exhibition
euronews.description: French President Emmanuel Macron will head to the Netherlands on Wednesday, before beginning his two-day trip to the UK.

euronews.title: Spain sheds almost 163,000 jobs in August as unemployment climbs
euronews.description: The Spanish economy lost 162,840 jobs last month with 44,419 registering as unemployed. The drop represents the smallest decrease in August since the Covid-19 pandemic.

euronews.title: British energy giant BP names Ian Tyler as chair after boardroom turmoil
euronews.description: British energy giant BP has appointed Ian Tyler as its permanent chair following the abrupt removal of his predecessor over governance and conduct concerns in May.

euronews.title: Signs before puberty could predict painful periods, study finds
euronews.description: A new study has found that non-painful symptoms in young girls, such as fatigue and dizziness, could help predict who is at risk of painful periods later on.

euronews.title: Sharp rise in utility bills pushes Russia's inflation further off target
euronews.description: The October increase follows a January rise and is the first double tariff hike in four years. The central bank warned it would push annual inflation further above its 4% target in an economy already squeezed by the costs of its war, sanctions and a 21% key interest rate.

euronews.title: Which EU countries have the most paid online subscriptions?
euronews.description: Nearly one in three Europeans paid for online subscriptions in 2025 according to data from Eurostat, but the continent is deeply split on its digital budget. Subscription services are particularly popular in northern and western households, while parts of Eastern Europe lag far behind.

euronews.description: NATO member Germany, which supports Ukraine in its fight against Russia, has long accused Moscow of targeting it with a campaign of hybrid attacks involving espionage and sabotage, claims the Kremlin has rejected.

euronews.title: Cargo ship with 10 crew sinks off Istanbul after collision, maritime authorities say

euronews.description: Apple Maps now shows Lake Ontario as "Lake America" for US users, following Google's lead in complying with US President Donald Trump's order as trade talks with Canada sour.

euronews.description: Star Trek fans are hoping to set a simultaneous Vulcan salute world record to celebrate the iconic show’s 60th anniversary next week.

euronews.description: Explosives experts from the State Criminal Police Office are searching the area around the site of the explosion.

lemonde.title: Jordan Bardella mal à l’aise pour défendre le programme présidentiel de Marine Le Pen sur le voile et les retraites
lemonde.description: En trois jours, le président du Rassemblement national a minimisé la portée de deux mesures symboliques défendues par les lepénistes, et a contredit la candidate sur le récit du départ de son conseiller, François Durvye.

lemonde.title: Les deux journalistes français détenus au Togo depuis la fin juillet, Gaël Mocaër et Sebastian Perez Pezzani, ont été libérés
lemonde.description: Gaël Mocaër et Sebastian Perez Pezzani, partis tourner un épisode de la série documentaire « Les Routes de l’impossible » sur France 5, avaient été arrêtés le 27 juillet. Ils sont poursuivis pour de supposées fausses déclarations liées à leur visa. Selon les informations du « Monde », ils devraient regagner la France dès mercredi soir.

lemonde.title: Joachim Nagel, président de la banque centrale allemande : « La hausse des taux sur les marchés financiers complique la situation de la BCE »
lemonde.description: Le président de la Bundesbank et candidat à la succession de Christine Lagarde à la tête de la Banque centrale européenne, explique, dans un entretien au « Monde », pourquoi il a soutenu la suspension du frein à l’endettement en Allemagne ou les emprunts européens communs, des prises de position surprenantes au sein de l’institution conservatrice.

lemonde.title: Jean-Paul Rappeneau, réalisateur de « Cyrano de Bergerac », est mort
lemonde.description: L’auteur de seulement huit films, qui a tourné avec les plus grandes stars françaises, est mort mardi 1er septembre à l’âge de 94 ans, a annoncé l’un de ses fils mercredi. Son « Cyrano de Bergerac » avec Gérard Depardieu a remporté 10 Césars dont celui du meilleur film en 1991.

lemonde.title: L’Iran réplique aux attaques américaines en visant des bases étasuniennes dans plusieurs pays du Golfe
lemonde.description: Téhéran a attaqué mercredi des bases américaines aux Emirats arabes unis, au Koweït et à Bahreïn, après la conclusion d’une deuxième salve de frappes lancées par les Etats-Unis. Quelques heures auparavant, le président iranien, Massoud Pezeshkian, avait plaidé pour une reprise des négociations.

lemonde.title: Dans le sud du Liban, des habitants désemparés, entre désarmement compliqué du Hezbollah et frappes israéliennes
lemonde.description: A Zaoutar El-Gharbiyé, Froun et Srifa, villes devenues « zones pilotes » en juillet, l’armée libanaise tente de se déployer, tandis que des habitants essaient de revenir dans leurs maisons détruites. Parallèlement, les bombardements israéliens se poursuivent à proximité.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre en Ukraine : la Russie affirme avoir frappé deux nouveaux centres logistiques près de Kiev
lemonde.description: Selon le ministère de la défense russe, un centre logistique de la société Raven Ukraine, situé près de Brovary, à l’est de la capitale ukrainienne, et un autre exploité par Stellar Jet, à Vychneve, ont été touchés à l’aide de drones Gueran-4 Seeker.

lemonde.title: « Le Monde » répond à vos questions sur sa ligne éditoriale, sa gouvernance et la vie de sa rédaction
lemonde.description: C’est la rentrée : comme chaque mois, Gilles van Kote, directeur délégué aux relations avec les lecteurs, répond en direct aux questions des internautes concernant la couverture de l’actualité et la vie du journal.

lemonde.title: « En Allemagne, un Land gouverné par l’AfD en ferait un laboratoire pour les projets du parti le plus radical des droites européennes »
lemonde.description: Outre-Rhin, le parti d’extrême droite Alternative pour l’Allemagne fait la course en tête en vue des élections des 6 et 20 septembre dans trois Länder. Son arrivée au pouvoir dans l’une de ces régions pourrait faire basculer le pays dans une crise sécuritaire et économique majeure, note, dans une tribune au « Monde », l’historienne Hélène Miard-Delacroix.

lemonde.title: Après l’accord pour la vente de SFR, Patrick Drahi continue de déconstruire son empire dans les télécoms
lemonde.description: Le milliardaire franco-israélien va céder ses parts dans une coentreprise d’Internet fixe en Allemagne, et est entré dans la dernière ligne droite pour vendre XpFibre, son vaste réseau de fibre optique en France.

lemonde.title: Présidentielle 2027 : les débats télévisés, source de tensions avant la primaire socialiste
lemonde.description: Les participants au scrutin réclament la tenue de trois débats avant le premier tour du 10 octobre, à l’exception de Raphaël Glucksmann qui plaide pour un rendez-vous unique en exclusivité sur le service public.

lemonde.title: En Espagne, le premier ministre, Pedro Sanchez, tente de reprendre la main sur la crise de Ceuta
lemonde.description: Face à une situation qui reste explosive dans l’enclave espagnole, l’exécutif multiplie les annonces : aide économique, hébergement d’urgence, visite du roi Felipe VI… Mais le chef du gouvernement ne parvient pas à éteindre une contestation qui gagne jusqu’à son propre camp.

lemonde.title: « Salvation », Grand Prix du jury à la Berlinale, une fable implacable sur la haine de l’autre et la guerre
lemonde.description: Le cinéaste turc Emin Alper, très critique à l’égard du régime du président Recep Tayyip Erdogan, tisse un récit fiévreux, à vocation universelle, dans le huis clos d’un village assiégé.

lemonde.title: Gaël Monfils passe le premier tour de l’US Open et fête ses 40 ans avec le public new-yorkais
lemonde.description: Le tennisman français, 311ᵉ mondial, a dignement célébré son anniversaire en éliminant le Paraguayen Adolfo Daniel Vallejo (60ᵉ) en quatre sets, dont un 6-0 pour finir la rencontre. Ses adieux en Grand Chelem attendront donc encore au moins un match de plus.

lemonde.title: « Nos responsables politiques continuent à traiter le dérèglement climatique comme une succession de crises »
lemonde.description: Face aux feux de forêt, indemniser et reconstruire ne suffit plus, car le réchauffement climatique atteint notre capacité à nous nourrir, à nous loger et à nous déplacer. Pour remédier à cette situation, les politiques publiques doivent être repensées, soutient Mathilde Durie, présidente du Centre des jeunes dirigeants, dans une tribune au « Monde ».

lemonde.title: IA au travail : une lente réglementation pour éviter les discriminations dans la gestion des ressources humaines
lemonde.description: Les entreprises sont déjà soumises à certaines interdictions réglementant leur usage de l’intelligence artificielle, comme le recours au traçage des émotions sur le lieu de travail, mais il faudra attendre la fin de 2027 pour que leurs obligations sur le sujet s’élargissent.

france24fr.description: Jean-Paul Rappeneau, réalisateur de "Cyrano de Bergerac", est mort à l'âge de 94 ans, a annoncé un de ses fils à l'Agence France-Presse. Il avait réalisé "Cyrano de Bergerac", qui avait remporté dix César en 1991, dont celui du meilleur film.

france24fr.title: Hong Kong : l'une des figures prodémocratie, Joshua Wong, plaide coupable de collusion
france24fr.description: Lors de son procès pour atteinte à la sécurité nationale, Joshua Wong, 29 ans, figure du mouvement prodémocratie à Hong Kong, a plaidé coupable mercredi de collusion avec l'étranger. Il purge déjà une peine de près de cinq ans d'emprisonnement pour subversion et risque désormais la prison à vie.

france24fr.title: Emmanuel Macron attendu à Londres pour dévoiler la tapisserie de Bayeux et rencontrer Andy Burnham
france24fr.description: Le président français est attendu, mercredi, à Londres pour dévoiler la tapisserie de Bayeux, prêtée au British Museum et exposée du 10 septembre au 11 juillet 2027. Emmanuel Macron doit également rencontrer le Premier ministre britannique Andy Burnham avant un entretien jeudi à Downing Street.

france24fr.title: Football : le Sénégalais Iliman Ndiaye transféré à Manchester City
france24fr.description: L’international sénégalais Iliman Ndiaye s’est engagé pour Manchester City. Il a signé un contrat jusqu'en 2031.

france24fr.title: Après neuf mois en mer, le porte-avions américain Lincoln fait escale à Pattaya en Thaïlande
france24fr.description: Le porte-avions américain Abraham-Lincoln est arrivé, mercredi, à Pattaya, en Thaïlande pour y faire escale après près de trois cents jours passés en mer. Il doit rester à quai jusqu'à dimanche. Le navire de guerre est par ailleurs au cœur d'une polémique sur les conditions de vie à son bord.

france24fr.title: États-Unis : Tyler Robinson, l'assassin présumé de Charlie Kirk, sera bien jugé
france24fr.description: Un juge de l'Utah a ordonné, mardi, le renvoi en procès de Tyler Robinson, 23 ans, accusé du meurtre du militant ultra-conservateur Charlie Kirk en septembre 2025. Le suspect, qui risque la peine de mort, a plaidé non coupable.

france24fr.title: Midterms 2026 : le vote par correspondance est en danger, avertit un lanceur d'alerte
france24fr.description: À deux mois des élections de mi-mandat aux États-Unis, un lanceur d'alerte affirme, mardi, que la Poste américaine a développé "en secret" des systèmes informatiques de manière "bâclée et précipitée" pour se conformer à un décret de Donald Trump visant à encadrer plus sévèrement le vote par correspondance. Des millions d'Américains pourraient ainsi être privés de bulletin de vote à distance.

france24fr.title: Au G20 Finance, les ministres plaident pour la liberté de navigation dans le détroit d'Ormuz
france24fr.description: À l'issue de deux jours de réunions au G20 à Asheville, les ministres des Finances ont défendu mardi une navigation sûre et sans coût dans le détroit d'Ormuz. La présence du ministre russe des Finances lors du sommet n'a "pas eu d'impact" sur l'issue des discussions, a affirmé le secrétaire américain au Trésor, Scott Bessent.

france24fr.title: Drones ukrainiens : Zelensky met en garde l'aviation civile, Poutine évoque une menace "terroriste"
france24fr.description: Le président ukrainien Volodymyr Zelensky a prévenu, mardi, l'aviation civile que "les jours sûrs dans le ciel russe sont révolus" en raison de l'intensification des frappes de drones ukrainiens sur la Russie. Son homologue russe Vladimir Poutine a qualifié cet avertissement de "déclaration de terrorisme d'État".

france24fr.title: Israël affirme avoir arrêté le chef de la sécurité intérieure du Hamas à Gaza
france24fr.description: L'armée israélienne a mené des frappes aériennes qui ont fait au moins quatre morts, mardi, dans la ville de Gaza. Lors de cette opération, Moueïn al-Arabid, le chef du service de sécurité intérieure du Hamas, a été interpellé à son domicile, a annoncé le Premier ministre israélien, Benjamin Netanyahu. Le mouvement islamiste a dénoncé une "opération criminelle".

france24fr.title: Tapisserie de Bayeux : les dessous d'une œuvre unique
france24fr.description: Emmanuel Macron est attendu, mercredi, à Londres pour l'inauguration de l'exposition consacrée à la tapisserie de Bayeux. Une œuvre monumentale vieille de presque 1 000 ans qui raconte la conquête de l'Angleterre par Guillaume le Conquérant.

france24fr.title: En direct : l'Iran attaque des bases des États-Unis après de nouvelles frappes américaines
france24fr.description: Jordanie, Irak, Bahreïn... L'Iran a attaqué, mercredi, des bases militaires des États-Unis dans le Golfe, après la conclusion d'une salve de frappes américaines contre lui, la deuxième en quelques jours. Les bombardements américains ont fait au moins 11 morts dans la République islamique, selon l'agence officielle Irna. Suivez notre direct.

france24fr.title: Lac Ontario ou Lac Amérique : Google a-t-il adopté la dénomination voulue par Trump ?
france24fr.description: Après avoir unilatéralement rebaptisé le golfe du Mexique en "golfe d’Amérique", Donald Trump s'attaque au Canada. Son récent décret visant à renommer le célèbre "lac Ontario" en "lac Amérique" a provoqué un véritable casse-tête pour les applications de cartographie comme Google et Apple Maps... et donné naissance à de folles rumeurs de représailles maritimes.

france24fr.title: Le Sénégal s'accorde avec le FMI sur un programme d'aide de plus de deux milliards de dollars
france24fr.description: Le FMI est parvenu à un accord avec le gouvernement du Sénégal en vue de la mise en place d'un programme d'aide "d'environ 2,2 milliards de dollars" pour la période 2026-2029, a annoncé le Fonds monétaire international. Cette annonce intervient près de trois ans après la suspension par l’institution de son dernier prêt, suite à la révélation par Dakar d’une dette cachée contractée par l’administration précédente.

france24fr.title: Basket : le champion de France Monaco exclu du monde professionnel
france24fr.description: Le champion de France en titre de basket, l'AS Monaco, exclu de la Ligue nationale de basket pour raisons financières, a annoncé mardi se porter candidat à une place dans le championnat de Nationale 1, le troisième niveau du basket français. La "Roca Team" espère rebondir et "retrouver sa place au sommet".

france24fr.title: Incursions de drones, sabotages, cyberattaques, espionnage : Moscou pousse-t-il l'Europe à bout ?
france24fr.description: Au lendemain d’une nouvelle attaque meurtrière sur Kiev et sa région, Volodymyr Zelensky a appelé ses partenaires à lui fournir davantage de capacités de défense balistiques. observador.description: O alerta do Mecanismo Nacional de Monitorização dos Direitos das Pessoas com Deficiência declara que o principal problema já não é a falta de leis, mas a sua aplicação desigual.

observador.title: Quase 10 mil infetados com cólera em Moçambique num ano
observador.description: Mais 150 novos casos e dois mortos num mês elevam para mais de 9700 infetados e 91 óbitos. Nações Unidas preveem financiamentos até 1,7 milhões de euros para intervenções rápidas.

observador.title: Portugal convoca embaixador russo após ataque na Alemanha
observador.description: Drone carregado com explosivos foi encontrado na área de operações de carga do aeroporto de Leipzig. Esta quarta-feira, o Ministro dos Negócios Estrangeiros convoca embaixador russo para explicações.

observador.title: Aquecimento global ultrapassará limite, mas pode ser contido
observador.description: António Guterres pede um redobrar dos esforços: acelerar a eliminação gradual dos combustíveis fósseis, promover a revolução das energias renováveis e reduzir drasticamente a poluição por metano.

observador.title: “Tirei carteira de músico para fazer carreira”
observador.description: Henrique Araújo, ex-presidente do Supremo Tribunal de Justiça, teve uma banda de rock, recusou-se a alterar um artigo chumbado pela Censura e foi fundador do PS em Arcos de Valdevez.

observador.title: Luís Neves, o Ranger do Texas
observador.description: Luís Neves quer ser um Ranger de Odemira, mas está é cada vez mais perto da porta de saída do Governo. Afinal irá o ministro aguentar a pressão da oposição?

observador.title: 9h. Ataques híbridos. Portugal convoca embaixador russo
observador.description: O anúncio é feito por Paulo Rangel, à entrada para uma reunião de Ministros dos Negócios Estrangeiros. Ainda a moção de censura ao Governo e a subida das temperaturas nos próximos dias.

observador.title: Amadora-Sintra. Doentes urgentes esperam 12 horas
observador.description: Doentes triados com pulseira amarela esperam mais de 12 horas para uma primeira observação médica. Ministra da Saúde admite que há uma elevada carência de médicos e enfermeiros no hospital.

observador.title: Seguro está à espera de quê para acabar com isto?
observador.description: André Ventura (que está a aproveitar o caso Luís Neves), o Presidente da República (que tem de agir) e Luís Neves (que fez mais uma vez declarações desastrosas) são o Bom, o Mau e o Vilão.

observador.title: Luís Neves: quem pára o ministro?
observador.description: Primeiro um tanque. Depois uma piscina. Em seguida apareceu um camião e perderam-se bidons. Agora Luís Neves interpela o líder da oposição. Quem pára este ministro em rota de colisão com a realidade?

observador.title: Bombardeamentos dos EUA causam pelo menos 18 mortos no Irão
observador.description: O Governo iraniano afirmou ter lançado uma "operação decisiva de retaliação", visando "as bases e os interesses norte-americanos na região" com mísseis e drones.

observador.title: Washington quer "muito investimento"em Caracas
observador.description: No aeroporto de Maiquetía, o secretário da Energia dos Estados Unidos disse aos jornalistas que pretende aumentar "o fluxo de capital privado de um grande número de empresas norte-americanas".

observador.title: As modelos em pobreza e os carrões dos ricos
observador.description: Investir na beleza para ser modelo e faturar só 100€? Vida difícil. E afinal, de onde vem esse "guito" todo para os carrões?

observador.title: Glória. Um ano depois, faltam indemnizações a vítimas
observador.description: Um ano após descarrilamento do elevador, a investigação ao acidente ainda decorre, bem como o apoio aos familiares das 16 vítimas mortais. Só quatro indemnizações foram concluídas.

observador.title: “Ainda há ‘druidas' a fazer oferendas ao deus Endovélico”
observador.description: Mafalda Santos, pintora artesanal na era digital, dirige a 24ª Bienal Internacional de Arte de Cerveira, a mais antiga da península, que este ano reflecte sobre “Territórios sem Fronteira"

observador.title: 8h. Ventura decide hoje se avança com moção de censura
observador.description: Ao final da tarde o líder do Chega revelou que ainda não tinha chegado a uma conclusão. Mais tarde, Ventura confirmou estar inclinado para avançar. Ainda, utentes esperam 11 horas no Amadora-Sintra.

observador.title: Luís Neves: afinal, quem pode usar bens apreendidos pela PS?
observador.description: Nesta newsletter encontra as notícias de que precisa para começar esta quarta-feira bem informado: da política à guerra, passando pelo desporto e pela cultura.

spiegel.title: Rüstung: U-Boot-Deal führt zu außergewöhnlich hoher Summe bei Waffenexporten nach Israel
spiegel.description: Noch 2025 galt teilweise ein Exportstopp, nun hat die Regierung Waffenlieferungen an Israel in Höhe von fast 800 Millionen Euro erlaubt. Ein Grund für die enorme Summe: ein verkauftes U-Boot.

spiegel.title: Klimakrise: Wer die Erde retten will, muss mehr anbieten als Daueralarm und Vorwürfe
spiegel.description: Die Erderwärmung braucht keine neue Schulddebatte, sondern eine positive Vision. Eine französische Forscherin sagt jetzt, wie diese aussieht.

spiegel.title: Jeanette Biedermann: Warum faszinieren uns späte Promi-Schwangerschaften so sehr?
spiegel.description: Jeanette Biedermann ist mit 46 Jahren Mutter geworden. Und die Welt guckt hin. Hinter dem Zauber stecken reaktionäre Geschlechterbilder – und die Frage, wer sich was leisten kann.

spiegel.title: Pete Hegseth: Der Fall Dan Driscoll offenbart das Versagen des US-"Kriegsministers"
spiegel.description: Donald Trumps Pentagon-Chef ist seit Langem umstritten. Nun wurde ihm auch noch Dan Driscoll abtrünnig, der Staatssekretär fürs Heer. Der Fall offenbart Pete Hegseths Versagen.

spiegel.title: Konjunktur: Wachstumsprognose von DIW mehr als verdoppelt
spiegel.description: Die Deutsche Wirtschaft erholt sich 2026 besser als gedacht. Das Deutsche Institut für Wirtschaftsforschung hat daher seine Wachstumsprognose deutlich erhöht. Doch eine große Schwachstelle bleibt.

spiegel.title: Kubicki-Kritiker Kuhle: FDP-Mann wird Gesellschafter beim Zentrum Liberale Moderne
spiegel.description: Es ist ein überraschendes Comeback: FDP-Mann Konstantin Kuhle wird nach SPIEGEL-Informationen Gesellschafter des Zentrums für Liberale Moderne. Der überparteiliche Thinktank wurde von prominenten Grünen gegründet.

spiegel.title: Anschlagsversuch in Leipzig: Kaja Kallas bestellt russischen EU-Gesandten ein
spiegel.description: Als Reaktion auf den Anschlagsversuch in Leipzig hat die EU-Außenbeauftragte den russischen EU-Gesandten einbestellt. Auch Frankreich und weitere Mitglieder der Europäischen Union zitierten die russischen Vertreter zum Gespräch.

spiegel.title: US Open: Alexander Zverev entgeht nur knapp dem Erstrunden-Aus
spiegel.description: Das war knapp: Fast fünf Stunden musste der bei den US Open Topgesetzte Alexander Zverev kämpfen, bevor er Außenseiter Lorenzo Sonego bezwungen hatte. Erst um 1.55 Uhr verwandelte der deutsche Tennisstar den Matchball.

spiegel.title: Uno sieht 1,5-Grad-Marke bald gerissen und gibt neues Ziel vor
spiegel.description: Ein Uno-Bericht erkennt erstmals an, dass sich die Erde in den kommenden Jahren um 1,5 Grad Celsius erwärmt haben wird. Generalsekretär Guterres sieht in Waldbränden und Überschwemmungen eine Warnung.

spiegel.title: Ägypten: 16 Tote und viele Verletzte bei Busunfall auf Sinaihalbinsel
spiegel.description: Zwischen den Touristenhotspots Dahab und Nuweiba ist ein Bus schwer verunglückt. Dabei kamen mehrere Menschen ums Leben, viele weitere wurden verletzt.

spiegel.title: Sachsen-Anhalt - News zur Landtagswahl im Blog: Deutsche-Bank-Chef warnt vor Aufstieg populistischer Parteien
spiegel.description: In Sachsen-Anhalt könnte die AfD die absolute Mehrheit erreichen. Der Deutsche-Bank-Chef Sewing mahnt, dass das dem Wachstum schade. Und: Merz schließt Koalition mit der Linken aus. Die Entwicklungen im News-Update.

spiegel.title: Deutsche Bahn: ICE-Tür öffnet sich während der Fahrt
spiegel.description: Ein Schnellzug der Deutschen Bahn musste in Unterfranken einen Nothalt einlegen. Eine Waggontür hatte sich während der Fahrt geöffnet. Die Polizei suchte nach möglicherweise aus dem Zug gestürzten Passagieren.

spiegel.title: Fahrradbranche verliert 2025 Umsatz und Stellen
spiegel.description: Auch wenn Rennräder und Gravelbikes gut laufen: Unterm Strich verzeichneten deutsche Fahrradhändler im vergangenen Jahr ein Minus. Neben Spätfolgen der Coronakrise kämpfen sie auch mit einer Nebenwirkung der US-Zölle.

spiegel.title: Hongkong: Demokratieaktivist Joshua Wong bekennt sich in weiterem Verfahren schuldig
spiegel.description: Joshua Wong sitzt seit 2020 in Hongkong im Gefängnis. Nun hat sich der bekannte Demokratieaktivist in einem weiteren Verfahren schuldig bekannt. Dem 29-Jährigen drohen weitere Jahre in Haft.

spiegel.title: Miley Cyrus heißt jetzt nur noch Miley
spiegel.description: Der US-Popstar macht es nun wie Zendaya, Beyoncé und Cher: Ihr Künstlername kommt künftig ohne Nachnamen aus. Im gleichen Schritt kündigt sie ihr zehntes Studioalbum an.

spiegel.title: Manchester City: Enzo Fernández wird für 145 Millionen Englands Rekordtransfer
spiegel.description: Enzo Fernández wechselt vom FC Chelsea zu Manchester City – für umgerechnet 145 Millionen Euro. So viel Geld hatte in England bislang nur Alexander Isak gekostet.

spiegel.title: Fall Jeffrey Epstein: Interview mit seiner ehemaligen Assistentin - »Ich war es gewohnt, zu gehorchen«
spiegel.description: Sie war Jeffrey Epsteins »Assistentin« und half, neue Opfer für ihn zu rekrutieren: Hier erzählt die Frau von der »Menschenhandels-Pyramide« und spricht über Manipulation und Schuld.

spiegel.title: Venezuela: Parlament und Armee billigen milliardenschweres Öl-Abkommen mit den USA
spiegel.description: Venezuela über die größten Ölreserven der Welt. Die Trump-Regierung hat nun Details zu dem Deal mit der Diktatur veröffentlicht. Das Verteidigungsministerium und das Außenministerium der USA spielen eine entscheidende Rolle.

elpais.title: Marlaska exige al director de la Policía que aclare si el cuerpo tiene información de que Marruecos estuvo tras el asalto masivo a Ceuta
elpais.description: El titular de Interior asegura en una carta a Pardo Piqueras que desconoce la información entregada a la Audiencia Nacional sobre la implicación de gendarmes marroquíes en los hechos del 30 de julio

elpais.title: Feijóo y Abascal unen fuerzas en una protesta que esperan masiva por la crisis de Ceuta
elpais.description: Los líderes de PP y Vox coincidirán en la concentración frente al Ayuntamiento de Madrid que la extrema derecha llama a secundar “contra el Gobierno traidor”

elpais.title: ¿Cómo han participado las redes rusas e israelies en la crisis migratoria de Ceuta?
elpais.description: La UE ha identificado intentos por parte de Rusia de sacar partido de la entrada de migrantes, aunque no disponen de pruebas que demuestren que esas campañas provocasen cruces masivos

elpais.title: Salir de Ceuta por su propio pie: “No puedo más, me voy. Aún no sé para qué vine”
elpais.description: La frontera entre la ciudad autónoma y Marruecos es un goteo diario de adolescentes que dejan voluntariamente la frontera tras “el peor mes de mi vida”

elpais.title: “La reacción de las autoridades marroquíes sobre Ceuta me parece vil”
elpais.description: Para Fouad Abdelmoumni, economista y activista marroquí, la crisis migratoria actual muestra que la frustración de sus compatriotas está mucho más extendida de lo que pensábamos

elpais.title: La Fiscalía Europea irrumpe en el ‘caso hidrocarburos’ y revela que Aldama y otros empresarios desviaron 27,9 millones a Portugal
elpais.description: La Fiscalía envía al juez de la Audiencia Nacional datos sobre la investigación portuguesa que alumbra el uso de empresas pantalla

elpais.title: La batalla de los mapas: Google y Apple cambian el lago Ontario por el lago América y se dispara la ‘app’ de su competidor
elpais.description: Donald Trump decidió cambiarlo de nombre por la disputa comercial con sus vecinos canadienses

elpais.title: Nelio Biedermann, el escritor de 23 años que narró un siglo entero: “Olvidar es una forma comprensible de sobrellevar la Historia”
elpais.description: En su novela ‘Lázár’, el autor se inspira en su familia de aristócratas húngaros para recorrer el convulso siglo XX. El resultado es un fenómeno literario traducido a más de 25 idiomas

elpais.title: Alejandro Betancourt, el nuevo oligarca latinoamericano de Trump
elpais.description: El empresario venezolano, investigado en Suiza y España, es la llave del acuerdo petrolero con el régimen de Rodríguez. Sus maniobras de los últimos años están sembradas de intrigas y negociaciones secretas

elpais.title: Romper la relación con la familia: por qué mucha gente apuesta por el contacto cero
elpais.description: El distanciamiento familiar por el que abogan figuras como Brooklyn Beckham comienza a ser habitual entre quienes quieren derrumbar el mito de que la familia debe mantenerse unida a toda costa

elpais.title: ‘American Horror Story’ en Disney+, ‘Babies’ en Filmin y otras series recomendadas para septiembre
elpais.description: Una selección de producciones de ficción destacadas este mes en plataformas

elpais.title: Qué comprar en septiembre en el mercado: higos, tomates, las primeras uvas y pescados azules para alargar el sabor del verano
elpais.description: En este mes conviven las últimas frutas del verano con las primeras verduras del otoño, junto a bonitos, sardinas y boquerones

elpais.title: En metálico, en efectivo, en numerario...
elpais.description: “¿Con tarjeta o con dinero?” Se entiende, pero es impropio: pagar con tarjeta también es hacerlo con dinero

elpais.title: Que Aristóteles no nos haga los deberes
elpais.description: La IA debe emplearse en la enseñanza para aprender a pensar mejor y no para evitar el esfuerzo personal

elpais.title: La regularización atenúa la pérdida de empleos en agosto con 162.800 puestos menos, pero acelera el paro
elpais.description: La destrucción de trabajo del octavo mes es la menor de los últimos años mientras el desempleo crece en 44.400 personas, el doble que en 2025

elpais.title: Estados Unidos vuelve a bombardear Irán, que responde con ataques contra sus efectivos en Jordania
elpais.description: Trump asegura que la negociación “es papel mojado” y amenaza con “mayores ataques” si Teherán responde

elpais.title: Alemania acusa a Rusia del ataque fallido con drones bomba en Leipzig
elpais.description: La policía halla explosivos y cohetes caseros en una subestación eléctrica clave para el funcionamiento de la mayor central térmica de Brandeburgo

elpais.title: Los interesados en comprar el polémico ático de la Comunidad de Madrid no pueden visitarlo
elpais.description: El Gobierno de Ayuso ha subido una nota a la web aclarando dudas en la que también indica que la terraza, originalmente de 200 metros, fue reducida a la mitad

nyt.title: At G20 Summit, Some U.S. Allies Push Back on Trump’s Economic Approach
nyt.description: At a summit meant to showcase President Trump’s economic policies as a model for the world, Europeans complained about tariffs and the war with Iran.

nyt.title: At G20 Meeting, Scott Bessent Accuses China of Flooding the World With Cheap Exports
nyt.description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent accused China for flooding the world with its cheap exports.

nyt.title: U.S. Strikes Iran Over Strait of Hormuz Mines, Trump Says
nyt.description: Iranian officials said the strikes caused significant damage, including killing four people and injuring several dozens at a wedding. Iran said it retaliated by firing on U.S. bases in the region.

nyt.title: U.S.S. Abraham Lincoln Docks in Thailand, Giving Weary Crew a Break
nyt.description: Thousands of sailors and Marines serve on the U.S.S. Abraham Lincoln, which came into the spotlight because of a tough deployment in the war in Iran.

nyt.title: Putin Pledges Increased Strikes in Ukraine and Support for Iran
nyt.description: The Russian president promised continued retaliation against the Ukrainians and “full solidarity” with Iran.

nyt.title: Woman Killed in Times Square Stabbing Identified as Bank of America VP
nyt.description: The New York Police Department made public the names of some of the people involved in a seemingly random knife attack on a crowded Manhattan street, but questions remained.

nyt.title: ‘Don’t Worry About Me’: Attacker’s Father Thought She Had Turned a Corner
nyt.description: Pamela Cisneros was killed by the police in Times Square after she stabbed two people, one fatally. Her father said she had stopped going with him to her mental health appointments.

nyt.title: Times Square Police Shooting Was Justified but Put Others at Risk, Experts Say
nyt.description: Officers who stood around a woman wielding two kitchen knives, and then opened fire without clearing the area, risked harming themselves or passers-by, the experts said.

nyt.title: Six Takeaways From the Massachusetts Primaries
nyt.description: Senator Ed Markey, 80, trounced a younger challenger who had made an argument for generational change. Two other longtime Democratic lawmakers hung on, too.

nyt.title: Longtime Democratic Congressman Defeats Progressive Rival in Massachusetts
nyt.description: Representative Stephen Lynch, 71, a centrist, beat Patrick Roath, 39, in a primary that reflected the party’s generational and ideological divides.

nyt.title: Former Biden White House Aide Wins Massachusetts Democratic House Primary
nyt.description: Dan Koh, who ran with the endorsement of former President Joseph R. Biden Jr., topped a crowded field to secure the nomination in the safely Democratic Sixth Congressional District.

nyt.title: House Censures Republican Accused of Sexually Harassing Two Aides
nyt.description: Representative Chuck Edwards received a formal rebuke on the floor after a speech in which he apologized for his conduct but said it did not constitute harassment.

nyt.title: On Trump’s Ballroom, Chief Justice Finds Himself in an Unusual Spot: In Dissent
nyt.description: Chief Justice John G. Roberts Jr. has been in the majority in divided cases more times than any other chief since 1953. But not this time.

nyt.title: Hegseth Targets 7 More Officers as His Frustrated Army Secretary Quits
nyt.description: The defense secretary’s cuts, which have hit about 10 percent of the military’s top officers, are dividing the Pentagon, officials said.

nyt.title: Carney Tells Trump Officials to ‘Stop Throwing Shade’ Over Canada-U.S. Trade Talks
nyt.description: Amid a trade war, Canada’s Liberals swept three special votes and new polling suggested strong support for Prime Minister Mark Carney and his retaliatory tariffs against the U.S.

nyt.title: Despite Duane Davis’s Conviction in Tupac Murder Trial, Some Still Seek Closure
nyt.description: When a man was found guilty of orchestrating the murder of Tupac Shakur, it brought catharsis to many who knew the rapper. But questions remain even after the trial.

nyt.title: A.I. Is to Be Banned in N.Y.C. Elementary and Middle Schools
nyt.description: A new policy to be announced by the Department of Education bars younger students from using A.I., but stops short of a moratorium.

nyt.title: Missouri Voters Appear to Recall City Councilman Over Data Center Support
nyt.description: Initial results showed that residents of Independence, Mo., voted overwhelmingly to recall an official who backed billions of dollars in tax breaks for a data center.

republika.title: Il Garante: “Tornano in aula 400 mila studenti con disabilità, ma a loro è negata l’inclusione”
republika.description: Maurizio Borgo spiega come la scarsità delle ore di sostegno, docenti di sostegno non specializzati, il 60 per cento della scuole non accessibili, la mancanza di rete lascino i diritti solo sulla carta

republika.title: Allarme di Tajani: “Possibili tentativi d’influenze russe sul voto in Italia”
republika.description: Il ministro degli Esteri: “È una questione che riguarda tutta l’Europa”. Su Vannacci: “Mi auguro non sia cavallo di Troia di Mosca”

republika.title: Le calciatrici spagnole aiutate dalla federazione se vorranno congelare gli ovuli
republika.description: La Rfef collaborerà con una clinica per la fertilità

republika.title: Militari in servizio nei comitati di Vannacci, scatta l’esposto: “Verificare i loro ruoli”
republika.description: Richiesto l’accertamento del ruolo di un carabiniere e di un militare dell’Aeronautica indicati come referenti di due comitati del movimento. Verifiche anche su eventuali altri uomini delle Forze armate coinvolti nella struttura politica.

republika.title: “Ink” di Danny Boyle apre Venezia: quando Murdoch inventò il giornale che somiglia ai social
republika.description: Il film apre Venezia con la storia del “Sun”: rotative, scandali, titoli urlati e una formula destinata a cambiare l’informazione

republika.title: A New York la giornata dell’orgoglio azzurro
republika.description: Grande prova degli italiani nel primo turno degli Us Open

republika.title: Sonego sfiora l’impresa: Zverev lo batte al quinto set agli Us Open. Vittorie per Musetti e Bellucci
republika.description: Grande match del piemontese, che ha avuto anche una palla break nel set decisivo ed è stato in vantaggio 2-1. Nessun problema per gli altri due azzurri, che non hanno concesso chances ai loro avversari

republika.title: George Clooney conquista Venezia: il premio alla carriera e sei giorni da star
republika.description: L’attore è sbarcato ieri con la moglie Amal Alamuddin nell’hotel già utilizzato per il matrimonio del 2014. Oggi il Leone alla carriera e un impegno al giorno tra panel e masterclass

republika.title: Barbera: “A Venezia nessuna bandiera, parleranno i film”
republika.description: Il direttore della Mostra sulle polemiche, la Palestina e l’intelligenza artificiale: “Va normata e controllata, ma può ampliare le possibilità creative”

republika.title: G20, la Cina fa muro: salta il comunicato congiunto. Dissidi su energia e commercio, irritazione Usa
republika.description: Dopo la presenza del ministro russo, un nuovo caso imbarazza il vertice di Washington sulle finanze mondiali. Bessent pubblica una dichiarazione presidenziale senza Pechino. Fonti americane: “Sono colpevoli”

republika.title: L’Europa e la Nato unite studiano la ritorsione: “Diamo a Kiev i beni russi”
republika.description: Rutte da von der Leyen: nuove sanzioni, sequestro dei 200 miliardi russi congelati e più intelligence contro le spie del Cremlino

republika.title: La lunga estate dei sabotaggi: così i paesi amici dell’Ucraina sono finiti nel mirino di Mosca
republika.description: La guerra “ibrida” diventa sempre più esplosiva. E punta direttamente alle industrie che forniscono aiuti militari a Kiev

republika.title: “Atti ostili pure qui in Estonia: Putin vuole che molliamo l’Ucraina, ma non cadiamo nella trappola”
republika.description: Il ministro degli Esteri Margus Tsahkna: “La Russia vuole convincere gli europei che sostenere Kiev ci renda meno sicuri: non dobbiamo cadere in questa trappola”

republika.title: Kuleba: “Putin non è uno stratega, ci bombarda per sopravvivere ed è capace di un’altra invasione”
republika.description: L’ex consigliere della diplomazia ucraina: “Resterà in guerra fino all’ultimo perché la trova conveniente come base ideologica, per reprimere il dissenso e consegnare l’economia agli amici”

republika.title: In Sassonia l’Afd punta a far dimenticare il nazismo: “Basta con arte e memoria”
republika.description: Al voto di domenica l’estrema destra può salire al potere per la prima volta dal 1945: insegnerà a “pensare tedesco”

republika.title: Tragedia di Roma, dalla nascita di Bianca ai colpi di pistola: gli anni d’inferno di Luca e Valentina
republika.description: La scoperta della disabilità della bambina, poi quella di non poter fare altri figli. E la rovina per avere cercato una cura fino all’ultimo

republika.title: I viaggi in Messico dal guru per Bianca: 300mila euro in fumo prima della strage in famiglia
republika.description: La piccola uccisa con un solo colpo, poi anche i genitori si sono sparati. La fortuna versata a un controverso medico messicano

npr.title: Israel bars U.S. citizens over criticism and ties to Palestinian activists, lawyers say
npr.description: Travelers from the U.S. and other nations are denied entry to Israel after interrogations about their links to Palestinians, plans to visit the occupied West Bank and opinions of Israel, lawyers say.

npr.title: Germany blames Russia for last month's attempted drone attack at Leipzig airport
npr.description: The German government blamed Russia for an attempted attack at Leipzig airport last month using a drone laden with explosives. It announced that it would shut down a Russian consulate among measures.

npr.title: Putin signals support for Iran in ongoing war with the U.S.
npr.description: Russia's Vladimir Putin is signaling unwavering support for Iran, as Tehran thanks Moscow for backing amid the escalating Middle East war.

npr.title: U.S. military strikes Iran, while Trump vows more for Tehran's retaliation
npr.description: The U.S. military hit targets in Iran on Tuesday and Tehran fired missiles and drones at various sites across the region in response as hostilities flare once again in an intermittent war.

npr.title: A week after the deadly floods in Nepal, rescuers work to find survivors
npr.description: Nearly a week after flash floods devastated parts of Nepal and Tibet, rescuers are still searching for people trapped in hydropower plants. But first they have to find the plants.

npr.title: SCOTUS allows Trump's ballroom project to continue. And, the Army secretary resigns
npr.description: The Supreme Court has ruled that President Trump's ballroom project may continue. And, Army Secretary Dan Driscoll resigns after 18 months on the job.

npr.title: Global finance ministers gather in North Carolina for G20 summit
npr.description: The U.S. is playing host to finance ministers from around the world this week. Russia's top economic official made a stir on Monday when he showed up in person at the meeting in North Carolina.

Sekeres, a scientist and former adviser, discusses the history and nuances of FDA oversight, including its process for screening advisory committee members for conflicts of interest.

proj-syn.title: Hard Lessons for Europe From the Ceuta Crisis
proj-syn.description: European Union leaders should have received several messages during the recent surge of migrants into the Spanish exclave of Ceuta. In particular, cohesion without trust is fragile; dependence without limits leads to vulnerability; and selective enforcement of international law risks eroding a pillar of Europe’s strategic identity.

proj-syn.title: The World’s Silent Majority for International Cooperation
proj-syn.description: The hollowing out of global institutions has resulted in a rapid loss of credibility for the international rule of law. But a majority of people worldwide still recognize the value of multilateralism, which countries can preserve in the absence of superpower consent by finding better ways to cooperate.

proj-syn.title: Building Canada’s Post-American Economy
proj-syn.description: Canada’s dependence on the US market has become a strategic liability, leaving it vulnerable to President Donald Trump’s bullying. Reducing that dependence will require building industries that can compete globally while removing the structural barriers that prevent innovative Canadian firms from scaling.

proj-syn.title: Trump and Xi Should Align on AI
proj-syn.description: When potential outcomes are systemic and irreversible, preparation must precede certainty. This is the logic behind insurance, as well as every pandemic plan and arms-control treaty ever created, and it must be the principle that guides our approach to AI—beginning at the upcoming US-China summit.

proj-syn.title: The Quiet Revolution in Services
proj-syn.description: While economists debate whether industrialization can still play its traditional growth-promoting role in the current global and technological context, services have unexpectedly become an engine for economic development around the world. For developing and developed economies alike, the timing could not be better.

proj-syn.title: AI Addicts Won’t Make Better Workers
proj-syn.description: Economists widely agree that AI will boost labor productivity. But this view does not account for the possibility that hyperscalers will go all out to get people hooked on LLMs, because the narrower applications for which these tools are actually useful do not justify the massive investments made so far.

proj-syn.title: Latin America’s Crime Tax
proj-syn.description: Even excluding lives lost, communities displaced, and families ravaged, the economic costs of organized crime in the region produce a bleak picture, shaving 0.5–2 percentage points off annual GDP growth in the most affected countries. That, too, represents a hefty human toll.

proj-syn.title: Are The Walls Closing in on Bessent?
proj-syn.description: Far from suggesting financial Armageddon, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent’s futile efforts to keep a lid on Treasury yields suggest that, once again, the dollar is America’s currency, but everyone else’s problem. But while investors have few alternatives, the bond-salesman-in-chief cannot be complacent.

proj-syn.title: AI Is Reviving Chinese Marxist Economics
proj-syn.description: As recently as two years ago, most Chinese economists paid only lip service to Marxism and assigned Western textbooks to their students. The advent of AI has changed that, because the technology—open source and available to the smallest manufacturer for a pittance—promises to avoid the “rent trap” common to capitalist economies.

proj-syn.title: Gen Z Is Transforming South Asia
proj-syn.description: Facing diminished economic prospects, many young people see not flawed institutions in need of gradual reform, but predatory systems robbing them of their future. Across South Asia, this sense has animated powerful protest movements, some of which could shape their countries' political trajectories for decades to come.

proj-syn.title: How Britain Can Help Build a Fairer Global Economy
proj-syn.description: With the United Kingdom poised to preside over both the G20 and the G7, Prime Minister Andy Burnham has a unique opportunity to usher in a new internationalism grounded not in military posturing, but in the pursuit of a fairer global economy. But he must abandon his predecessor’s defensive approach.

proj-syn.title: Technocracy Can’t Fix Europe
proj-syn.description: A new private initiative bringing together the crème de la crème of European business, financial, economic, and tech elites could well prove useful in kick-starting European growth and innovation. But first, it must recognize that the problem it hopes to solve is fundamentally political.

proj-syn.title: The Fed and the Treasury Are in Denial
proj-syn.description: For most of the postwar era, the United States has enjoyed a privileged position as an issuer of both sovereign debt and US dollars that always found takers. But the US may no longer be able to rely on stable demand for its debt or its currency, forcing policymakers to face the truth about how financial markets are made.

proj-syn.title: To End Global Hunger, Invest in Rural Communities
proj-syn.description: Even as hunger declines around the world, food insecurity remains prevalent in rural communities. Restoring soil health, expanding access to new technologies, strengthening land rights, and upgrading public infrastructure are essential to boost agricultural productivity and protect rural livelihoods.

proj-syn.title: The Sanctions Illusion
proj-syn.description: Those who defend sweeping financial sanctions against countries like Russia and Iran often claim that popular suffering is a defensible means of pressuring the target government. But while such measures certainly inflict widespread suffering on civilian populations, this rarely translates into political change.

proj-syn.title: Is Monetarism Making a Comeback?
proj-syn.description: After decades on the margins of mainstream economic thinking, monetarism is beginning to re-enter the debate, most notably at the Federal Reserve. To regain credibility, however, monetarists must learn from past mistakes and adapt to the monetary and financial realities of the 21st century.

proj-syn.title: China’s Super-Dam Is Becoming an Upstream Water Bomb
proj-syn.description: The latest evidence suggests that the Chinese scientific establishment understands the dangers of a planned Himalayan dam—the world's largest—more clearly than its political leadership is willing to acknowledge. With the livelihoods of two billion people at stake, the international community needs to weigh in.

proj-syn.title: Europe and the War in Ukraine
proj-syn.description: If Europe remains a mere collection of small states and middle powers, the current period of profound geopolitical and historical change will also mark the end of its role on the world stage. With no end in sight for Russia's war in Ukraine, Europeans must come to grips with reality.
